mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05) in the identified regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In the specified regime, the 20-day SPX returns show no correlation (R-squared < 0.05) with the combined PAYEMS/UNRATE interaction signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% suggests expanding economic activity, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 20 consecutive months of INDPRO > 2% monthly growth, 5-day SPX forward returns show no positive trend relative to INDPRO growth (Mann-Kendall test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 0.5% over two months indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to raise rates, which in turn produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by > 0.5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In the identified regime, the 20-day SPX returns are positively correlated (R-squared > 0.2) with CPIAUCSL changes, contradicting the mechanism's prediction.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of RSAFS to GDP (implied credit demand) exceeds 110% for three consecutive months, it reflects an over-stretched credit market that tends to trigger a sharp S&P 500 decline in the following 60-day window.
failure_condition: The 60-day SPX returns show no significant negative relationship with the RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio in the specified regime (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% followed by a sustained rise in labor participation (HOUST) suggests a demographic or confidence-driven labor market expansion, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% and HOUST increases by > 5,000 in the following month
failure_condition: In the regime described, the interaction of UNRATE and HOUST does not predict SPX returns (R-squared < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) combined with flat or declining industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a supply-side soft landing, which historically precedes a mild S&P 500 rally of up to 3% over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases for 4 consecutive months while INDPRO remains flat or declines
failure_condition: Over 60 days, SPX returns show no statistically significant positive relationship with the CPIAUCSL/INDPRO interaction (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a tightening cycle defined by two consecutive increases in FEDFUNDS above 5%, the discount rate premium embedded in equity valuations rises, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases for two consecutive months above 5%
failure_condition: In the identified regime, the 5-day SPX returns are not significantly different from the pre-tightening period (p > 0.05).
